name: s5-symbiont-to-organelle
title: S5 — From symbiont to organelle: when does integration become heritable?
concept: Inheritance and evolutionary individuality made operational as fidelity of symbiont partitioning, vertical transmission, and host-symbiont fitness alignment. An evolutionary/population model coupled to multi-generation agent-based host/symbiont division, gene-function exchange, and stochastic partitioning.
question: Which routes to gene loss, transfer, and protein import lead to stable inheritance and irreversible dependence? Distinguish mere within-host survival from vertical transmission over many generations, gene-function rescue, and sustained fitness alignment.
hypothesis: Stable heritable integration requires high-fidelity vertical transmission AND host-symbiont fitness alignment together; gene loss becomes irreversible (partner-removal lethal) only after transmission fidelity crosses a threshold. Within-host survival alone does not produce a new evolutionary unit.
claim: Integration becomes heritable and coordinated — a new evolutionary individual emerges — only when vertical-transmission fidelity and host-symbiont fitness alignment both cross threshold, after which gene loss is irreversible and the partner becomes obligate; configurations with survival but low transmission fidelity do NOT cross into heritable individuality.

behavior_tests.name: heritable-integration-stable
behavior_tests.description: Vertical-transmission fidelity stays high across many generations (stable inheritance).

provenance.note: Fraction of daughter hosts retaining a viable symbiont over >=50 generations; >0.95 = stable vertical inheritance. Threshold pre-registered; refine against population-genetics theory.

behavior_tests.name: dependence-irreversible-after-gene-loss
behavior_tests.description: After modeled gene loss, partner removal becomes lethal (obligate dependence).

literature_anchors.expectation: FECA-LECA transition frames where a new eukaryotic individual emerges.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: Composite NOT yet built. Requires: a multi-generation agent-based host/symbiont division process with stochastic partitioning, a gene-loss / rescue process, and a population-genetics selection layer; a within-host-survival-only control.

data_inputs.name: EukProt v3
data_inputs.use: extant eukaryotic proteomes for ancestral comparison
